## In plain English

Cutting a release today always maps a stable X.Y.Z tag to npm latest. v0.128.0 was meant for maintainers only and still moved latest; the fix was manual dist-tag surgery. Prefer-A lets the release skill choose the dist-tag (default latest), carries that choice into the publish workflow, widens version validation for non-latest prereleases, and keeps both packages on the same tag. Non-latest messaging and GitHub Latest flag stay footnote-class unless Round-1 proves they change fail-closed association.

## Approaches

### Approach A (Prefer-A lean)
- Phase 1 / CLI: choose dist-tag (latest | maintainer | beta | …) with latest default; thread into release metadata the workflow can read.
- npm-publish.yml: honor explicit dist-tag (tag-push carrier + workflow_dispatch dist_tag input); keep SemVer auto-derive when unset; refuse tags that are valid version ranges.
- validateVersion: allow X.Y.Z-beta.N (and peer prerelease forms the skill already understands) when chosen dist-tag is not latest; keep strict X.Y.Z for latest.
- One shared DIST_TAG for @deftai/directive and @deftai/directive-runtime.
- Footnote: non-latest release notes / Slack install line / GitHub make_latest=false.

### Approach B
- Encode channel only via prerelease version suffix (rely on existing auto-map). Does not cover stable X.Y.Z to maintainer.

### Approach C
- Docs + manual npm dist-tag after publish. Already failed for 0.128.0.

## Proposed Bound remedy (draft — bind after Round-1)

- relieves: P1 — Skill/CLI dist-tag choice at version gate (default latest) threaded into durable release metadata the publish path reads
- relieves: P2 — npm-publish.yml honors explicit dist-tag (carrier + workflow_dispatch input); auto-derive only when unset; refuse version-range dist-tags
- relieves: P3 — validateVersion admits prerelease forms when dist-tag is not latest; latest keeps strict X.Y.Z
- relieves: P4 — Single shared DIST_TAG for directive + directive-runtime on every publish path
- Footnote: non-latest notes/Slack @<dist-tag> install line + GitHub release not Latest

## Reject

- Approach B version-suffix-only (no stable→maintainer)
- Approach C post-publish manual dist-tag as the primary close
- Softening npm irrevocability disclosure / release-publish grant
- Different dist-tags per package in one cut
- Allowing dist-tags that are valid version ranges

## file_scope (lean)

- content/skills/deft-directive-release/SKILL.md (and packs source if packs:render owns it)
- packages/core/src/release/version.ts (+ tests)
- packages/core/src/release/main.ts and adjacent release CLI flag plumbing as needed
- .github/workflows/npm-publish.yml
- packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/npm_publish_workflow.test.ts

## Keep-outs

- #5365 Environment/trusted-publisher / prepare-vs-OIDC split (already shipped)
- #5805 pin-only execution close (pin already must include the change)
- #5848 / #2354 except as related cites
- Softening tag-push npm irrevocability or authz:grant release-publish
- Inventing a second npm publish workflow

### F1 — blocks-the-design: resolve channel before the tag-triggered publish
P1/P3. At the pin, release/pipeline.ts creates/pushes the tag in Steps 10–11 and creates the GitHub release afterward; npm-publish.yml resolves DIST_TAG before checkout. “Durable release metadata” alone permits a GitHub-release carrier that does not yet exist when npm starts. Remedy: choose one tag-bound carrier available at push (for example, a structured annotated-tag field), resolve it before packing, and distinguish legacy absence from malformed declared metadata. Reject malformed/conflicting channel data; auto-derive only for genuine absence. Define dispatch-input precedence explicitly. Treat input as data via environment/argv, never shell-evaluated text; validate npm tag syntax and reject valid version ranges before output/publish. This changes the mechanism, so bind it, not merely a docs reminder.

### F2 — blocks-the-design: dispatch override can split a partially published cut
P1/P3 and the shared-channel invariant. Both OIDC publish steps already consume the SAME prepare.outputs.dist_tag: no separate per-package selector exists. However, each catches a publish failure and accepts npm view PKG@VERSION as success. If runtime already shipped on maintainer and launcher failed, a retry overriding to beta skips the existing runtime without retagging it, then publishes launcher to beta. Shared input is not proof of shared registry outcome.
Remedy: preserve the recorded channel on retries and reject conflicting overrides before publishing; an already-published package must satisfy the selected channel postcondition, not just version existence. Keep manual channel promotion outside this cut path. This is a concrete retry constraint on the existing mechanism, not a second publish workflow.

P2. version.ts:70 rejects everything except strict X.Y.Z; release/main.ts:28 AND release-publish/main.ts:32 call it. Updating only the cut CLI leaves beta publication refused at the later GitHub visibility step. Include release-publish channel recovery/validation from the same carrier; keep latest strict and preserve the release-publish grant and npm irrevocability disclosure. Test stable/maintainer and beta/beta through both entry points, plus prerelease/latest refusal. Prefer-A can bind with this explicit scope.

Stop 1 P2 is version validation, P3 is workflow selection, and P4 is consumer-latest presentation. The draft swaps P2/P3 and labels the already-shared DIST_TAG invariant P4. Correct those references. No extra Bound limb for wording or label repair.

Suggested short Bound: (1) persist and resolve one validated tag-bound channel before publish, with legacy-only fallback and retry consistency; (2) apply channel-aware version validation across cut and publish commands; (3) feed the one resolved channel to both packages and verify retry postconditions. P4 presentation remains the attached footnote. Dry-run must show both package names and the resolved channel.

Road not taken: prerelease-suffix-only is simpler and reuses today's auto-map, but cannot satisfy stable X.Y.Z to maintainer; it would become sufficient only if that requirement were withdrawn. ### F1 — blocks-the-design — the P4 limb cites an invariant that already holds; Stop 1 P4 ships unrelieved

Evidence. `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` L303 sets a single job-level `DIST_TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.dist_tag }}` on `publish`, and both publish steps (L334, L347) read that same `"${DIST_TAG}"`. `npm_publish_workflow.test.ts` already asserts exactly two `npm publish` commands. There is no per-package divergence path at tip to close.

Failure mode. The draft maps P4 to "single shared DIST_TAG for directive + directive-runtime on every publish path" and moves Stop 1's actual P4 — a non-latest cut still presenting as consumer-latest — wholesale into the footnote. Bound binds, the `P4` cite resolves against a pre-existing invariant, and the v0.128.0 operator still hand-fixes the GitHub release afterwards.

Disposition consequence. As written the `P4` cite is not honest relief. Re-point the limb before bind.

Remedy (short). Make the P4 limb the GitHub release channel flag: `createGithubRelease` (`packages/core/src/release/gh.ts` L65-82) already takes a typed `options.prerelease` and pushes `--prerelease`; thread `distTag !== "latest"` into the sibling not-Latest flag at that same push site. Keep the shared-`DIST_TAG` invariant as a fixture assertion (both publish commands read the same `${DIST_TAG}`; no per-package `--tag` override), not a Bound limb. Note `packages/core/src/release/gh.ts` is absent from the draft file_scope.

On the #3368 line: the release-notes wording and the Slack `@<dist-tag>` install line are dispose-wording and stay footnote — correct. The GitHub "Latest" flag is not wording. It is a typed field that re-points a machine-readable channel pointer, in the same class as the npm dist-tag this ticket exists to control. Split the current single footnote in two rather than promoting all of it.

### F2 — blocks-the-design — the dispatch re-publish path silently re-derives `latest`

Evidence. The identity step (L43-102) derives `DIST_TAG` from `VERSION` alone: stable `X.Y.Z` to `latest` at L85. `workflow_dispatch` is documented at L16-19 as the manual re-publish of an existing tag after a failed tag run, and the publish steps swallow the already-published case (L334, L347). The draft's P2 limb keeps "auto-derive only when unset" with `dist_tag` as an optional dispatch input.

Failure mode. Stable `X.Y.Z` is cut to `maintainer` through the carrier. The tag run partially fails. The operator re-dispatches the same tag and leaves `dist_tag` empty — the field is optional and the tag already "knows" its channel. Auto-derive returns `latest`. Whichever package had not yet published publishes to `latest`. That is the v0.128.0 incident reproduced through the re-publish door, on the very path the Bound adds.

Disposition consequence. The Bound does not fail closed on its own new surface. Two carriers for one fact is the defect; an optional second carrier is the sharp edge.

Remedy (short). The carrier is authoritative on both triggers. `dist_tag` input is admitted only when the tag carries no dist-tag; a carrier/input mismatch fails the run. "Auto-derive when unset" then means carrier-absent, not input-absent.

### F3 — blocks-the-design — the carrier cannot be read where the draft implies, and the obvious placement precedes the ancestry control

Evidence. The identity step is L43, the first `actions/checkout` in `prepare` is L104, and "Peel tag SHA and verify master ancestry (#5365)" is L109. The `prepare` job's `dist_tag` output is wired to `steps.identity.outputs.dist_tag` at L40. Identity runs with no repository content at all. The release pipeline stages only `RELEASE_ARTIFACTS = ["CHANGELOG.md", "ROADMAP.md"]` (`packages/core/src/release/constants.ts` L33) into the release commit.

Failure mode. An in-tree carrier is unreadable at identity time, so the natural fix is a carrier read wired into or beside identity — which resolves the publish channel from tag content before the #5365 ancestry peel has verified that tag. Injection/swarm lens fires here: tag content is pushed input feeding a publish-authorization decision, and the control that constrains it sits two steps later.

Disposition consequence. The Bound must name where the carrier is read, not only that one exists; the ordering is the fail-closed property.

Remedy (short). Resolve the carrier in a step after the peel/ancestry verification and re-point the `prepare` job `dist_tag` output (L40) at that step; identity keeps the SemVer derive as fallback. ## Problem
The release skill (`deft-directive-release` / `task release`) can't choose which npm dist-tag a release publishes to. The tag is derived automatically in `.github/workflows/npm-publish.yml` (the "Resolve tag name, SemVer, and dist-tag (#5365)" step): a stable `X.Y.Z` always goes to `latest`, and a prerelease goes to its prerelease id or `next`. `workflow_dispatch` only takes `tag`, with no dist-tag input.

The release CLI also only accepts strict `X.Y.Z` (`packages/core/src/release/version.ts`, `validateVersion`: `/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`), so a `-beta.N` cut is refused before it reaches the workflow.

v0.128.0 shows the gap. It was meant for maintainers only, but the workflow published it to `latest`. The dist-tags had to be fixed by hand afterwards (`latest` back to 0.127.0, plus a new `maintainer` tag pointing at 0.128.0).

Both packages' npm trusted publishers (`@deftai/directive`, `@deftai/directive-runtime`) are already set up to allow publishing to any dist-tag.

## Ask
Let the release skill choose the dist-tag, e.g. `latest`, `maintainer` or `beta`, with `latest` as the default.

- **Release skill:** add a dist-tag choice at the version gate. Pass it through to the tag or release metadata.
- **npm-publish.yml:** honor an explicit dist-tag from the release (and add a `dist_tag` input to `workflow_dispatch`). Keep the npm rule that a dist-tag can't be a valid version range.
- **Both packages:** publish the runtime and main package to the same dist-tag.
- **Prereleases:** allow prerelease versions (`X.Y.Z-beta.N`) in `validateVersion` when the dist-tag isn't `latest`, so betas can go through the skill. Note: per the pin-only design (#5805), the change only takes effect for releases cut from a pin that already includes it.
- **Non-latest releases:** for a non-`latest` dist-tag, the release notes and Slack template should say who the build is for and give `npm i -g @deftai/directive@<dist-tag>` instead of `@latest`, and the GitHub release should not be marked "Latest".

## Acceptance
- A dry run shows the chosen dist-tag for both packages.
- Cutting a stable version to `maintainer` leaves `latest` unchanged.
- Cutting `X.Y.Z-beta.N` to `beta` works end to end.
- Releases with no dist-tag chosen behave exactly as today.

Related: #5365, #5848, #2354.
